name: Hodaviah
title: Descendant of the royal line of Judah
summary: Hodaviah is a person mentioned in several contexts in the Bible, most known from the genealogies in 1 Chronicles and the book of Ezra. He was a descendant of David's royal line through Zerubbabel, and his descendants were among the Levites who returned from exile in Babylon. The name means 'praise the Lord' and testifies to faith and worship during a time of rebuilding.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Judah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hodaviah is mentioned as a descendant in the tribe of Judah, linking him to the royal Davidic line.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among Benjamin's descendants
keyEvents.description: A person named Hodaviah is mentioned among the descendants of the tribe of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: A Hodaviah is mentioned as a family head in the half-tribe of Manasseh, a leader among his people.

keyEvents.title: The Return of the Levites from Exile
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Hodaviah were among the Levites who returned from the Babylonian exile under Zerubbabel and played a role in rebuilding the temple.

keyEvents.title: Recorded in Nehemiah's Census
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Hodaviah are also mentioned in Nehemiah's list of those who returned to Judah after the exile.
